description: Shared Renovate preset of the ioanalytica repositories: one pull request per update, each with a review request, no update that waits on the Dependency Dashboard, security fixes at any time. A repository extends it with github>ioanalytica/renovate-config and keeps its own managers, groups and notes.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: A fix for a known vulnerability comes at once: outside the nightly schedule and without the three days' wait.

packageRules.description: A digest has no release date to age against: with minimumReleaseAge, its pull request would stay pending for good (minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour timestamp-required).

What a repository publishes does not wait: an update of something its images or charts contain (a pin under docker/ or chart/, in a Dockerfile, Chart.yaml or values.yaml at the top) comes in the night after its release. Most security fixes of such components are in no database that would make them a vulnerability alert. Packages from npm and PyPI keep the three days: there a release that is pulled again in its first days is the more likely trouble, and their known vulnerabilities come as alerts at once.

A new major is a decision, not routine: its pull request comes at once like any other and carries the label decision. Closing it declines every release of that major (the next major comes again), unless the pull request is an immortal group, which Renovate opens again.

A new digest under the same version of an action means its release tag was moved: look at the commit before merging. An image of a workflow's services or container is not meant: its new digest under the same tag is a rebuild.
prBodyNotes: The tag of this action now points to another commit. Look at that commit before merging; close the pull request to keep the old one.

packageRules.description: A repository pins this preset by tag and its pin-checksums workflow by commit: both move to a new release of ioanalytica/renovate-config in one pull request.
